edits.content:
# E02 — Phase-4 type-aware eviction paired ablation

## Objective

Measure the reversible, opt-in, non-safety component `phase4-type-aware-eviction` against `phase4-fifo` on the production `RuntimeMemoryStore`. This is an internal evaluation only: product defaults, product locks, approval behavior, and user-visible behavior remain unchanged.

## Pre-registration

The fixture is `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json`. It is local and deterministic, permits no provider, and contains at least 20 cases, three repeats per condition, one shared seed, a fixed insertion order per case, and separate stores for every observation.

Primary metrics and regression budgets are registered before execution in the fixture:

- success rate and pass@1/pass@2/pass@3 using the E01 convention;
- p50 and p95 latency;
- token proxy;
- false blocks;
- safety violations;
- paired effect size and a 95% confidence interval.

The report must include both conditions and treatment-minus-baseline effects. Zero and negative effects are valid observations. No winner may be selected after seeing results.

## Execution contract

1. Construct a fresh production `RuntimeMemoryStore` for each case, repeat, and condition.
2. Probe that the store is empty and isolated.
3. Insert fixture items in the fixed order.
4. Run baseline FIFO and treatment type-aware eviction as a leave-one-out comparison; do not mix policies in one store.
5. Capture retained and evicted identifiers. At least one pair must differ; otherwise execution fails as an ineffective or miswired treatment.
6. Record success, false-block, and safety-violation outcomes plus latency and token-proxy observations.
7. Pair observations by case and repeat, aggregate the registered metrics, bootstrap paired differences with the fixture seed, and calculate paired Cohen's dz.
8. Check the preregistered regression budget without changing it.

## Reporting

Publish the complete report, including negative or zero estimates and confidence intervals. State explicitly that the experiment is internal and does not authorize a default, lock, or approval change.

## Completion gates

- Fixture validation succeeds.
- All 20 or more cases complete in both conditions for all three repeats.
- Store isolation and retained/evicted difference checks pass.
- Runtime/core type checks and scoped lint pass.
- Harness validation and dry-run pass.
- Credential scan has zero matches.
- `SHA256SUMS` is readable and covers the candidate artifacts.
- README translations are reviewed; no change is required because there is no user-visible change.

# Paired-ablation boundary rule

## Allowed evaluation

An E02 candidate may evaluate `phase4-type-aware-eviction` as an explicitly opt-in treatment against `phase4-fifo` as baseline on isolated production `RuntimeMemoryStore` instances. It may use deterministic local fixtures with no provider and may produce an internal report.

## Required invariants

- The treatment and baseline must use the same case, repeat, seed, insertion order, fixture, and store configuration.
- Every observation must use an isolated store. Stores must not be reused across conditions or cases.
- A run must verify that retained or evicted sets differ at least once. Failure to do so is a wiring failure, not evidence of equivalence.
- The report must contain success, pass^k, p50/p95 latency, token proxy, false blocks, safety violations, paired effect sizes, and 95% intervals.
- Metrics and budgets must come from the preregistered fixture. Effects are treatment minus baseline.
- Zero and negative effects must be retained and reported without reinterpretation.

## Forbidden changes

This evaluation must not change product defaults, product locks, approval behavior, safety enforcement, permissions, dependencies, runtime/core production behavior, or user-visible surfaces. A beneficial result is an internal report only and does not authorize promotion.

The candidate must not invoke a real provider, use credentials, access the network, read tests at runtime, or perform network/process side effects. Credential scanning must report zero matches. Candidate artifacts must be covered by a readable `SHA256SUMS` manifest.

## Review

Runtime/core types, scoped lint, fixture validation, harness validation/dry-run, credential scanning, checksum readback, and the four README languages are review gates. If the component is absent, inert, non-reversible, safety-critical, or not wired to the real store, the candidate fails the boundary and must not be described as an ablation of the production component.

# E02 paired ablation closure — Phase-4 type-aware eviction

## Scope

This package closes the internal evaluation gap for the reversible, non-safety, opt-in `phase4-type-aware-eviction` component. The production consumer is `RuntimeMemoryStore`. Baseline is the preceding Phase-4 FIFO behavior; treatment is a leave-one-out type-aware policy. No product default, lock, approval rule, safety control, permission, dependency, or user-visible behavior is changed.

## Experimental design

The deterministic fixture contains 20 cases, three repeats, two conditions, and paired seed `42002`. It has no provider (`allowedProviders: ["none"]`). Each case has a fixed insertion order. A fresh `RuntimeMemoryStore` is required for every case/repeat/condition and is checked for isolation before execution.

The preregistered primary measurements are success and pass@1/pass@2/pass@3 (E01 convention), p50/p95 latency, token proxy, false blocks, and safety violations. Paired differences are treatment minus baseline. The report includes paired Cohen's dz and deterministic paired-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (10,000 resamples). The latency, token, false-block, and safety budgets are fixed in the fixture before execution.

## Effectiveness and removal trace

Before aggregating metrics, the harness compares retained and evicted identifiers for each paired condition. At least one pair must differ. If no pair differs, the run is rejected as miswired; it is not reported as evidence that the policies are equivalent. The comparison is retained in the report so the removal trace is auditable.

## Interpretation

All estimates are reported exactly as observed. Zero and negative treatment effects are valid results. Confidence intervals are descriptive uncertainty estimates and do not justify selecting a winner after seeing the fixture. A favorable result is an internal report only and grants no approval to change defaults or locks.

## Verification gates

Before closure, run the targeted candidate tests, runtime/core type checks, scoped lint, fixture validation, harness validate and dry-run, credential scanning, and `SHA256SUMS` readback. The credential scan must have zero matches and all candidate files must be represented in the checksum manifest. Review README files in all four maintained languages; they require no edit because this package has no user-visible effect.

## Artifacts

- `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.mjs`: fixture validation, paired execution, metrics, bootstrap interval, effect size, budget check, and effectiveness trace.
- `scripts/lib/paired-ablation.d.mts`: public types.
- `shared/agent-dev/paired-ablation-fixture.json`: deterministic local fixture and preregistration.
- `harness/specs/tasks/harness-gap-paired-ablation.md`: task and completion contract.
- `harness/specs/rules/paired-ablation-boundary.md`: boundary and prohibited changes.
